title: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for trilateral talks with the US and Russia in October
body:
On 4 October 2026, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at a news conference in Kyiv with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz that Ukraine was ready for trilateral talks with the United States and Russia that month. He said Washington was pushing for technical-level talks by the end of October. The United Arab Emirates, which hosted earlier talks, could host again, and Zelensky said Kyiv was open to meeting there or in another country proposed by the American side.

Al Jazeera reported that US ceasefire efforts had been paused since Washington launched its war on Iran. On 13 September, the Kremlin had said it did not rule out three-way talks that month. On 1 October, Russian President Vladimir Putin had ruled out a ceasefire with Ukraine in a speech in Moscow.

Zelensky said both sides were stepping up long-range attacks, and that Russia was targeting Ukraine's energy sector before winter. He accused Russia of hitting civilian infrastructure, including data centres and mobile network facilities. Separately, Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said India wanted a larger mediating role and was discussing grain and energy exports and Black Sea shipping.
